article_content: Julie Sculley got married in a hotel that looks like a castle — but that wasn’t the fairy tale she was there to witness. The 37-year-old mother from Framingham, Massachusetts, took the day off work to watch Prince William and Catherine Middleton tie the knot. Like countless wedding enthusiasts and Anglophiles, she rose before dawn, settled onto her living room couch, and watched as the bride made the magical transition from commoner to Duchess of Cambridge. She may have shed a tear or two. 'The anticipation kind of catapulted me into this somewhat weepy state,' she admitted after a bit of prodding. By all accounts, Sculley was in good company. Countless Americans across the country woke unusually early to mark the occasion. Some hosted royal-themed parties with tea, scones, and even exaggerated British accents. 'There’s something about William and Catherine,' Sculley said. 'It’s so romantic, and I love all the tradition. It’s just not something you get to see every day.' Down south in Atlanta, Sally Gachunji rose at 4 a.m. ET to catch every moment — from the wedding dress to the bride’s walk down the aisle at Westminster Abbey. 'I’m actually on a conference call with some pals. Oh, my God, did you see those hats?' she exclaimed breathlessly. 'I can’t miss it. This is history. It’s an opportunity to watch a modern-day fairy tale.' Across town, Christy George, 41, gathered with a group of friends — nicknamed 'the duchesses' — in Marietta. Dressed in elegant frocks and fancy hats, they nibbled on cucumber sandwiches while waiting for the royal couple’s first public kiss. 'It’s like a fairy tale, an escape from ordinary life for a while,' George said, adjusting her light purple hat adorned with a flower. She noted that Americans, despite fighting a war to escape British rule, remain fascinated by royalty. 'We don’t have that here,' she said. 'I remember watching Princess Diana’s wedding too.' At George’s gathering, guests competed in a hat-making contest; the winner received a replica of Princess Diana’s ring. Royal fans found Catherine especially relatable. 'She’s a commoner who fell in love with a prince,' said Gachunji, sipping tea. 'For a romantic like me, that’s huge.' To enhance the experience, she spoke to friends in a playful British accent, using phrases like 'cheerio' to say goodbye. In Tennessee, Dena Oneal woke at dawn and had to convince her husband and two sons to give up the remote. 'They didn’t want to watch at first,' the Murfreesboro resident said. 'But it’s a once-in-a-lifetime event. Seeing the carriages, the hats, the ceremony — it became a royal education for them.' Lise Caldwell, a 37-year-old freelance writer from Indiana, set her alarm for 4:45 a.m. The night before, she visited a friend’s house to bake scones. They enjoyed them with cream and jam during the broadcast. 'I was a little girl when Charles and Diana got married,' she recalled. 'I was obsessed. I wanted to see their son get married.' 'I’m a grown woman now,' she added. 'I know it’s a little ridiculous to get up for someone else’s wedding — but it’s fun.' Jennifer Slocumb of Roswell, Georgia, appreciated the pageantry as a welcome distraction from domestic politics. 'We don’t see the costs or the politics,' she said. 'We just see a handsome man and a beautiful woman, all dressed up.' Businesses nationwide capitalized on the event. The Ritz-Carlton in Georgetown hosted a royal viewing party with overnight stays, cocktails named after the couple, and engraved champagne flutes — plus an iPad interactive feature to enhance the experience. In New York, Trinity Church, chartered by King William III in 1697, screened the wedding. On the West Coast, Madame Tussauds Hollywood held an all-night viewing starting at 1 a.m., featuring live broadcast with wax figures of Elton John and David Beckham — each worth $300,000. 'It’s a once-in-a-lifetime chance to experience history,' the museum said. (The real Beckham and John attended the ceremony in London.) Globally, an estimated 2 billion viewers tuned in, according to British Culture Secretary Jeremy Hunt. In the UK, street parties took place amid tight security due to threats from extremist groups. Yet, royal enthusiasm was more subdued among Britons: fewer than half planned to watch, and 56% said they weren’t interested. Back in the U.S., the cost of devotion was simple: exhaustion. 'I might take a nap later today,' said Sculley, who woke at 4:15 a.m. 'I’m a bit tired.'

article_content: The grieving mother of British doctor Abbas Khan broke down at his crowded funeral at Regent’s Park Mosque in London, crying out in despair: 'Nobody helped me. I love my son. I am the loser. I’m the failure.' As mourners tried to comfort her, she pleaded: 'I beg everyone. I touch every foot. Please give me back my son.' Dr. Khan, a 32-year-old orthopaedic surgeon from London, was arrested in November 2012 in Aleppo, Syria, after traveling from Turkey to treat victims of hospital bombings. He died in custody on December 17, 2013. While the Syrian government claimed he took his own life, his family insists he was murdered. At the funeral, his brother Shahnawaz Khan delivered an emotional tribute, calling Dr. Khan 'our star' and 'the kindest and simplest man I’ve ever met.' He recalled their childhood bond and lamented the cruelty of losing him just before he was due to be released. Family members revealed a letter written by Dr. Khan expressing hope that he would return home for Christmas. His widow, Hanna, and their two children, Abdullah (age 6) and Rurayya (age 7), were present. The funeral attracted hundreds, reflecting widespread public sympathy. Family solicitor Nabeel Sheikh praised the overwhelming support and confirmed a coroner’s inquest would open the following day at Walthamstow Coroner’s Court. Sheikh also criticized the UK government, stating the family had received no meaningful assistance—only a letter from the Prime Minister after the tragedy. They had repeatedly sought meetings with Foreign Secretary William Hague without success. An imam honored Dr. Khan as a martyr who gave his life in service to others. Chaplain Karimah Bint Daoud noted that in the Muslim community, 'when one is killed, it affects us all,' explaining the large turnout. Dr. Khan’s body was taken to Ilford, East London, for burial. The inquest, set to begin on Friday, aims to establish the true cause of his death—and whether justice can be achieved.

article_content: Car insurance fraud is common, but a suspected scammer in South Korea has taken it to an extreme new level. A dash cam video posted online shows a man deliberately running into a moving car, smashing his head against the windshield — hard enough to shatter the glass — in what appears to be a staged accident to claim compensation. The footage, recorded on September 19, begins with a routine scene: a driver exiting a parking lot. Suddenly, a pedestrian darts into the road, sprinting toward the vehicle. Inside the car, occupants react in panic as the man leaps onto the hood and slams his head into the windshield. The glass cracks, and he collapses onto the pavement. The act, clearly intended to trigger an insurance payout, has labeled the man an 'insurance scammer' in online descriptions. This incident underscores a growing crisis: according to the Insurance Research Centre, an average of 156 people are caught daily in car insurance fraud schemes in South Korea. Over the past five years, these scams have cost more than KRW1.18 trillion (approximately AU$1.8 billion). Meanwhile, dash cams are gaining global traction. In Russia, they are so ubiquitous that owning one can reduce car insurance premiums. In February 2023, dash cams captured a meteor streaking across the sky — footage that went viral. Similarly, earlier this year, a dash cam in Brisbane recorded a cyclist being struck on a highway, proving their value as impartial witnesses.

article_content: After being told he wouldn’t feature regularly under new Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal, midfielder Tom Cleverley secured a season-long loan move to Aston Villa — a decision made in the final hours of the transfer window. Cleverley, 25, reached out directly to Villa boss Paul Lambert after growing frustrated with his lack of playing time, despite having won a Premier League title and earned 13 England caps in recent years. He dismissed the harsh criticism he received online, pointing out that no player thrives under constant negativity — especially during a trophyless season at United. 'You don’t become a bad player because of a tweet,' he said. 'Everyone in the squad felt it. It wasn’t just me.' While Everton manager Roberto Martinez, who previously coached Cleverley at Wigan, expressed interest in signing him on loan, he claimed United effectively shut the door — not because Cleverley was unavailable, but because they reportedly didn’t want to strengthen a rival club that finished above them in the league last season. Cleverley admitted his agent, Simon Kennedy, nearly derailed the deal by secretly involving Everton without informing Villa. Cleverley is now focused on proving himself at Villa Park, aiming to help the team climb back into the Premier League’s top half and eventually earn another call-up to the England squad. His debut against Liverpool will be emotionally charged, as he returns to a stadium where he spent 14 formative years — but this time wearing a different color. Despite the turbulence surrounding his exit, Cleverley remains grounded: 'The only opinion that matters is my manager’s. Football is full of noise — but results speak louder.'

article_content: Cesc Fabregas received a yellow card during Chelsea’s 1-1 draw with Southampton at St Mary’s, as his team pushed for a winner. With the score level in the 60th minute, Fabregas was brought down in the penalty area by Southampton rookie defender Matt Targett. As the ball bounced between them, Targett’s right foot appeared to make contact with Fabregas, causing him to fall. Despite visible contact, referee Anthony Taylor waved away penalty appeals and booked Fabregas for simulation. Replays confirmed that Targett’s leg made contact as Fabregas controlled the ball. Moments later, an angry Fabregas kicked the ball away in frustration — a reaction that drew further scrutiny. Sky Sports pundit Graeme Souness stated, 'We all know it’s a penalty and the referee got it wrong.' The incident adds Fabregas to a growing list of Chelsea players — including Willian, Gary Cahill, Diego Costa, and Branislav Ivanovic — criticized under Jose Mourinho for alleged diving. Mourinho looked visibly upset as the yellow card was shown.

article_content: In a global survey of 25,000 people across 23 nations, actress, filmmaker, and humanitarian Angelina Jolie emerged as the world’s most admired woman — surpassing icons like Nobel laureate Malala Yousafzai, former U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, and even Britain’s long-reigning monarch, Queen Elizabeth II. The YouGov poll, conducted in 2014, revealed that Jolie’s tireless advocacy for refugees and her critically acclaimed direction of the film 'Unbroken' resonated deeply with international audiences. Malala, the young Pakistani activist who survived a Taliban assassination attempt and became the youngest-ever Nobel Peace Prize winner, came in second. Hillary Clinton followed closely in third place. Yet within the United Kingdom, the results painted a very different picture. British respondents placed Queen Elizabeth II at the top of their list, narrowly beating acclaimed actress Judi Dench. Jolie, despite her global fame, landed only seventh among UK respondents. Other notable placements included Celine Dion in sixth globally — a surprising nod ahead of Oprah Winfrey and Julia Roberts — and Burmese democracy icon Aung San Suu Kyi and German Chancellor Angela Merkel rounding out the top ten. The poll underscored a striking trend: global admiration often leans toward entertainers and celebrities rather than political leaders. Figures like Taylor Swift and Beyoncé ranked eleventh and twelfth, outpacing several heads of state. In the UK, regional favorites such as Scotland’s First Minister Nicola Sturgeon and TV host Ellen DeGeneres cracked the top ten, reflecting local cultural preferences. Among men, Microsoft founder Bill Gates was globally the most respected, while physicist Stephen Hawking earned the top spot in Britain. Royal family members also fared well: Prince William ranked fifth internationally, ahead of his brother Prince Harry in eighth. David Beckham landed tenth, while political figure Nigel Farage came in eleventh. Michelle Obama, admired alongside her husband Barack Obama, secured fifth place globally — a rare instance where both spouses appeared in their respective top ten lists.

article_content: In a remarkable turn of events, more than 270 artworks long thought lost or unseen by the public have surfaced in France — all attributed to Pablo Picasso. The discovery came after Pierre Le Guennec, a 71-year-old retired electrician living near the French Riviera, mailed the Picasso Administration dozens of photos of pieces he claimed were gifted to him by the artist during the final years of Picasso’s life. When he later delivered the full collection — including cubist collages, ink drawings, lithographs, notebooks, and a watercolor — experts from the estate confirmed they were genuine. But instead of celebration, controversy erupted. In September, Claude Picasso, the artist’s son, along with five other heirs, filed a lawsuit accusing Le Guennec of stealing the works. Authorities seized the entire collection in early October and are now holding them in a secure vault near Paris. While the Picasso family acknowledges the pieces are authentic, they question how Le Guennec obtained them. His explanation — that Picasso personally gave him the art over three years — lacks documentation, and legal representatives argue such a massive, undocumented transfer defies logic. No prior record links Le Guennec closely to Picasso, and the sheer volume of works raises red flags. Still, Le Guennec maintains he never stole anything. As investigations continue, the case has become a puzzle: if the art is real, how did it leave the artist’s hands? And if it’s stolen, where did it go between 1973 and now?

Yet, he still incurred $1.5 million in private jet expenses during his bid for the White House. DeSantis, widely viewed as Donald Trump’s main rival in the GOP primary, trails the former president by wide margins in national polls. According to third-quarter financial filings released Sunday, his campaign spent nearly as much as it raised. As reported by Politico, while some campaign travel was conducted on commercial flights, the campaign also spent $1.5 million on private jets during the quarter. Payments were made to at least six private aviation providers: Advanced Aviation Team, Avion Aviation, Empyreal Jet, IsraJets, N2024D LLC, and Silver Air Private Jets. The Washington Post noted that most private flights ceased in July and August, with only one IsraJets charge appearing in September. One commentator offered a critical assessment, suggesting DeSantis’ major misstep was aligning his campaign and public image with fringe online figures known as 'groypers'—a decision that highlights poor judgment and undermines his electability.

article_content: In 2009, two-year-old Georgia Keeling from Norwich died after being misdiagnosed with swine flu during the height of the H1N1 pandemic. She was actually suffering from a rare and aggressive group A streptococcal infection — a form of blood poisoning that can lead to meningitis. On August 4, 2009, paramedic Patricia Perfect visited the family home after an emergency call. After a 45-minute assessment, she concluded Georgia had swine flu and prescribed Tamiflu. Despite the child’s worsening condition, Perfect did not arrange immediate hospital transport, believing the case fit the pandemic pattern. Four hours later, after a second 999 call, Georgia was rushed to the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital — but she died on arrival at 4:24 p.m. At the subsequent inquest, coroner William Armstrong delivered a narrative verdict, stating Georgia’s death resulted from an 'erroneous diagnosis' and failure to recognize the severity of her condition. He emphasized that immediate hospitalization would have significantly improved her chances of survival. Medical experts testified that Georgia’s symptoms — including fever and rash — were inconsistent with typical swine flu and clearly indicated a life-threatening illness. Dr. Jeffrey Perrin noted multiple 'red flag' signs were missed. Paramedic Perfect expressed regret, acknowledging that while she followed guidelines, the overwhelming focus on swine flu at the time clouded her judgment. She stated, 'Had that not been a factor, I would have been looking at other reasons.' The East of England Ambulance Service has since apologized, retrained staff, and partnered with the international Surviving Sepsis Campaign to improve recognition of critical pediatric infections. Dr. Pamela Chrispin, medical director, confirmed these reforms are now standard practice. Georgia’s parents, Natasha Keeling and Paul Sewell, described the past three years as 'going through hell.' Yet they welcomed the ambulance service’s apology and reforms, stating: 'We were failed by one person — not the entire NHS.' They hope Georgia’s story will prevent similar tragedies.

article_content: By Daniel Bates. PUBLISHED: 11:00 EST, 11 December 2012. | UPDATED: 16:51 EST, 11 December 2012. Justin Bieber’s Twitter tribute to six-year-old cancer victim Avalanna Routh was the most retweeted tweet of 2012. The pop star’s heartfelt message — 'RIP Avalanna. I love you' — was retweeted 223,771 times by his fans. The second most shared tweet came from Michael Jackson fans @obeyMJ: 'R.I.P. Whitney Houston. Retweet for respect,' with 191,043 retweets. Touching tribute: Justin Bieber’s message about the death of six-year-old brain cancer victim Avalanna Routh became the most retweeted post of 2012, reaching nearly 224,000 shares. Angel: The pop star posted photos of himself with Avalanna shortly after she lost her battle with cancer. On Twitter’s official 2012 statistics list, British boy band One Direction topped the charts for follower growth. Band members Harry Styles, Louis Tomlinson, Zayn Malik, Liam Payne, and Niall Horan saw the largest increases in followers among all celebrities. Niall Horan recorded the biggest surge, gaining 712% more followers to reach 8.2 million. Liam Payne followed with a 608% increase to six million, while the band’s official account, @onedirection, grew by 605% to 6.7 million. Louis Tomlinson gained 587% more followers (5.8 million), and Harry Styles rose by 493% to also reach 6.7 million. Bieber remained the most Tweeted-about celebrity overall, followed by Horan, Styles, and Zayn Malik. Twitter’s end-of-year report revealed that the MTV Video Music Awards were the most-Tweeted event of the year, generating 14.7 million tweets and 52 million fan votes. Whitney Houston’s death on February 11 triggered 10 million tweets — peaking at 73,662 per minute. Bieber’s fans were deeply moved by Avalanna’s passing. The child, who had brain cancer, met Bieber after her parents launched a Twitter campaign to connect with him. He affectionately called her 'Mrs. Bieber' and shared photos of them hugging, playing board games, and eating cupcakes. Avalanna died on September 26, 2012. Three days later, during a concert in Glendale, Arizona, Bieber dedicated a song to her. His full tweet read: 'Just got the worst news ever. One of the greatest spirits I have ever known is gone. Please pray for her family and for her... RIP Avalanna. I love you.' The third most retweeted tweet came from Harry Styles on the night of the VMAs: 'We owe you everything. Thank you so much for this. Three VMAs!! YEAH .xx' Other notable tweets included Ben Savage announcing his role in the 'Boy Meets World' revival (114,179 retweets) and Niall Horan marking the band’s second anniversary (103,772 retweets). Twitter senior manager Rachael Horwitz told USA Today that Bieber’s message 'was something beyond his music' — it was 'him and his fans saying goodbye to one of their own,' and it clearly resonated globally. She added that one of Twitter’s greatest strengths is enabling intimate, one-on-one conversations between fans and celebrities who would otherwise feel unreachable. Popular shows and films trending on Twitter in 2012 included Family Guy, American Dad, Hey Arnold, American Idol, Pretty Little Liars, 106 & Park, SNL, The Fresh Prince, Boy Meets World, Think Like a Man, The Hunger Games, The Avengers, Red Tails, 21 Jump Street, The Dark Knight Rises, Dark Shadows, The Devil Inside, and Safe House.

article_content: Best-selling author Jennifer Egan is enjoying an extraordinary week. Her novel, 'A Visit from the Goon Squad,' won the Pulitzer Prize, secured a potential TV adaptation with HBO, and earned her a place on Time magazine’s list of the 100 Most Influential People. In an interview with CNN, Egan reflected on her journey, describing how the idea for the novel began with a simple observation: a wallet left unattended in a hotel bathroom. That moment sparked a cascade of fictional questions — who would take it? Why? — leading to the creation of a complex, interwoven narrative. One of the novel’s most striking features is its PowerPoint chapter. Inspired by a 2008 article about the Obama campaign’s use of PowerPoint as a strategic tool, Egan wondered if the software could serve as a medium for fiction. Though she initially wrote the chapter by hand — lacking the software on her laptop — she eventually realized that PowerPoint’s fragmented, slide-based structure mirrored the novel’s nonlinear form: disconnected moments that coalesce into a larger story. Egan emphasizes that while her characters are entirely imagined, she must deeply empathize with them to write authentically. 'There’s some of me in all of them,' she says, explaining that understanding their inner logic — however strange — is essential. She writes all her fiction by hand, preferring to lean back in a soft chair during morning hours — often napping mid-sentence. Journalism, however, is composed on a computer. Her literary influences range from Proust and Woolf to Dickens and Ursula Le Guin, whose works she’s currently rereading with her 10-year-old son. Looking ahead, Egan hopes to return to a long-delayed project: a historical novel set in New York during and after World War II, centered on the women who worked in the Brooklyn Navy Yard — welding, riveting, and building ships, only to be dismissed when the men returned home. She has interviewed many of these women firsthand as part of an oral history project, and she aims to honor their stories through fiction. Beyond the Pulitzer, 'A Visit from the Goon Squad' has also won the National Book Critics Circle Award and was a finalist for the PEN/Faulkner Award, the LA Times Book Prize, and the UK’s Orange Prize.

article_content: Rolf Harris, a once-beloved entertainer, was sentenced to five years and nine months in prison for twelve counts of indecent assault, including attacks on children as young as eight. Among the victims are Vanessa Feltz and Linda Nolan, who have publicly shared their harrowing experiences. Feltz revealed that during a live 1996 broadcast of Channel 4’s The Big Breakfast, Harris sexually assaulted her while her wife watched and the crew filmed. She described feeling his hand move up her leg beneath her dress until it reached her underwear. With no other option, she requested an ad break to escape him. She later contacted police but was told the allegation was too late to add to the existing case. Linda Nolan recounted being molested at age 15 in 1975 while touring South Africa with her singing sisters. Harris, she said, attacked her backstage while she wore only a dressing gown, kissing and touching her before dismissing it as a joke. 'Don’t be silly, I’m only giving you a hug,' he told her. In total, fifteen new allegations have emerged from victims in Britain, Australia, and New Zealand, potentially opening new avenues for legal action. Public institutions and private individuals are severing ties with Harris’s legacy. Artworks he created—including a portrait of Bonnie Tyler—have lost up to 90% of their value. Some owners now contemplate destroying the paintings. Museums have removed his name from plaques. Universities have revoked his honorary degrees. Despite his crimes, some artifacts linked to Harris’s family—such as a photograph taken by his grandfather, George Frederick Harris—are being preserved, distinguishing between personal history and personal guilt. Feltz and Nolan’s courage in speaking out aims to empower others to come forward, challenging the culture of silence that once protected predators like Harris.

article_content: The University of New Mexico’s women’s soccer team is under investigation following a team initiation event on Sunday night that left two players hospitalized. Reports indicate that new members were forced to undress, had urine poured over them, and were compelled to consume large quantities of alcohol. In response, the university has suspended all team activities and opened an internal review. Two individuals linked to the team have departed from UNM. While police responded to the scene and transported the injured athletes to the hospital, no criminal investigation is currently underway — though authorities say they may act if evidence reveals violations of existing laws like assault or reckless endangerment. New Mexico is one of only six U.S. states without a specific anti-hazing statute, meaning prosecutions would rely on broader criminal codes. The university has stressed that photographs circulating online — including a team photo from April — do not depict anyone involved in the incident and must not be used to falsely identify suspects.

article_content: Launched in 1995, the Airbus A330-200 is a modern twin-engine jet and a cornerstone of Airbus’s long-haul fleet. It boasts a range of 12,500 kilometers (6,750 nautical miles) and can carry up to 253 passengers. Widely trusted by airlines around the world, over 600 A330-200s are currently in service with 82 carriers—including Air France—and Airbus holds another 300 orders. Aviation expert Kieran Daly described the aircraft as 'reliable, ultra-modern, and state-of-the-art,' noting its impeccable safety record. He emphasized that the only recorded crash involving this model occurred in 1994—during testing, before commercial service began. The crash resulted from extreme maneuvers performed by test pilots, not a design flaw. The aircraft is powered by dependable General Electric CF6 engines and features advanced avionics and communication systems. Air France Flight AF447, en route from Rio de Janeiro to Paris, transmitted an automated warning of electrical issues amid severe turbulence early in its 11-hour journey. Despite this, experts say such weather alone is unlikely to cause total system failure in a modern wide-body jet. Former Airbus pilot John Wiley added that lightning strikes, while dramatic, do not typically bring down contemporary airliners. The flight’s captain had over 11,000 total flight hours, including 1,700 on the A330/A340. Both first officers had extensive experience on the same aircraft, with 3,000 and 6,600 hours respectively. The aircraft itself had logged 18,870 flight hours and underwent its last scheduled maintenance just two days before departure. The larger A330-300, introduced in 1993, shares this strong safety profile. In 2001, an Air Transat A330 glided nearly 18 minutes after dual engine failure over the Atlantic, successfully landing in the Azores. In 2008, Qantas Flight 72—an A330-303—made an emergency landing in Australia after a sudden altitude shift injured 74 passengers. The cause of that incident remains under investigation.

article_content: Tony Abbott's personal approval rating has suffered another decline, as national support for the Federal Government fell three percentage points to 37%, according to the latest Newspoll. The drop was particularly steep in key states: Western Australia saw a six-point slide to 40%, while Queensland dropped four points to 37%. Support among women has fallen two points to 35%, while men continue to back the government at higher levels. Abbott’s standing as preferred Prime Minister has plummeted across all demographics and regions. He now trails Labor leader Bill Shorten 37% to 41% nationally — a four-point gap widening from previous polls. In Abbott’s home state of New South Wales, 42% prefer Shorten over Abbott’s 38%. Support among voters aged 50 and older has dropped from 48% to 45%, and among those aged 35–49, it fell three points to 34%. These results follow Abbott’s controversial remarks at the Melbourne Institute, where he described pre-colonial Australia as 'unsettled' or 'scarcely settled,' suggesting the nation’s foundation stemmed from British colonial enterprise. His comments sparked widespread backlash and intensified scrutiny over his leadership.

article_content: Usain Bolt has resumed intensive training, committing to two sessions per day in preparation for the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The six-time Olympic gold medalist is working hard to regain peak form after taking nine weeks off following foot surgery. 'It’s been tough, but I’ve been through this before — I know what it takes to come back,' Bolt said. 'I’m pushing forward to do what’s necessary for this season.' While Bolt could have pursued an individual spot in the 100m or 200m, he chose not to take a position from fellow Jamaicans who earned their places at the national trials. Instead, he’ll focus on the 4x100m relay, aiming to contribute to Jamaica’s team effort. 'I’ve always wanted to run at the Commonwealth Games,' he added. 'Now that I’m getting back into shape, I see myself competing in the relay. I’m going there for my fans — to show them I’m returning, and to give them hope for what’s ahead.' Bolt also commented on the handling of the ban involving American sprinter Tyson Gay, stating that officials sent a 'bad message to the sport.' In Glasgow, Bolt’s image is featured on a public mural alongside British legends Sir Chris Hoy and Mo Farah — a tribute to his enduring legacy in athletics.

article_content: A retired engineering inspector, Alexander Paton, is set to stand trial accused of committing triple bigamy. Between 2006 and 2012, the 68-year-old allegedly married three women while still legally married to his first wife, Dorothy Campbell. Paton is accused of marrying Perla Montilla, a 65-year-old Filipino mortgage funder, on October 14, 2006, at the registrar’s office in Glenrothes, Fife — despite being already married to Campbell. He reportedly lived with Montilla as her husband. Less than a year later, on June 20, 2007, Paton allegedly married Judit Gherghiteanu, a 67-year-old Romanian engineer, at the same Glenrothes registry office — still legally married to Montilla. On July 14, 2012, he is further accused of marrying Margaret Nicol, a 66-year-old woman from Fife, at Prospecthill Christian Fellowship Church in Greenock, Renfrewshire — again while still married to Montilla. Paton appeared at Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court, where he pleaded not guilty to all charges. Sheriff Kevin Veal adjourned the case for trial on December 12, with a preliminary hearing scheduled for November 29. Veal indicated Paton’s attendance at the trial date may be excused unless a plea is reached earlier. In Scotland, bigamy is treated as a criminal offense involving fraud against the state, disrupting official records, and potentially undermining inheritance and estate laws. If the second spouse was unaware of the prior marriage, the act may also constitute fraud by deception.

article_content: The family of murdered British soldier Fusilier Lee Rigby attended a heartfelt charity truck pull in Medbourne, Leicestershire, to support his young son and local causes. Rigby, 25, was brutally killed in a terrorist attack outside Woolwich Barracks in southeast London in May 2013. His widow, Rebecca, and their two-year-old son, Jack, watched as teams from his regiment pulled eight-ton trucks along a one-mile course through the village. Hundreds of locals gathered in the sunshine to cheer on the participants, many wearing tribute shirts bearing Rigby’s name. Proceeds from the event will benefit a fund established for Jack Rigby’s future, as well as community projects in Medbourne. Rebecca Rigby described the day as 'a great turnout' and said it helped keep her husband’s memory alive. Among those lending support were actor Rupert Grint, known for his role in Harry Potter, and singers Smith and Jones from BBC’s The Voice. Organizer Gary Gardner called it 'the biggest event Medbourne has seen in years,' urging the community to come together in solidarity. Michael Adebolajo, 28, and Michael Adebowale, 22, have been charged with Rigby’s murder and are scheduled to stand trial at the Old Bailey on November 18, following a preliminary hearing on September 27. Earlier, Mail Online published touching, previously unseen photos of Rigby holding Jack in his army uniform and in a Manchester United shirt.

article_content: NEW DELHI: The Burman family, promoters of Dabur, has filed a formal complaint with securities regulators alleging that Rashmi Saluja, Chairperson of Religare Enterprises Ltd (REL), sold shares shortly after being informed of their intent to launch an open offer for a controlling stake in the company. According to the complaint, Saluja sold 12.93 lakh shares — representing 0.4% of REL’s total equity — on September 21 and 22, just one day after a meeting with Burman representatives on September 20. During that meeting, the Burmans disclosed their plan to acquire an additional 26% stake through a Rs 2,116 crore open offer, increasing their total holding to 47.24%. The Burman-controlled entities — MB Finmart, Puran Associates, VIC Enterprises, and Milky Investment and Trading Co — sent a letter to SEBI and India’s stock exchanges (BSE and NSE), expressing concern over what they describe as a suspicious timing of the transaction. However, REL and Saluja strongly deny the allegations. In a statement, REL clarified that the share sale was part of a long-standing Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) process initiated months before the September 20 meeting. The sale involved Saluja and 12 other employees, all of whom had received necessary approvals well in advance. Mohit Burman, Chairman of Dabur India, expressed surprise at REL’s reversal in stance. While REL initially welcomed the open offer, it later criticized the Rs 235-per-share price as undervalued. REL shares were trading at Rs 221.85 on the BSE at the time of reporting. Burman also criticized REL’s board structure, noting the absence of shareholder representatives despite the company being fully owned by shareholders. He questioned why independent directors, who had previously thanked the Burmans for their July investment, suddenly raised objections only after the open offer was announced. The Burmans assert they acted transparently, notifying REL of their intentions ahead of time to avoid surprises. They emphasized they have no intention of replacing the board post-acquisition and are awaiting regulatory clearances from SEBI, RBI, and IRDAI, which they expect within the next three to four months.

article_content: Claudio Bravo has arrived at FC Barcelona following Chile’s exit from the 2014 World Cup. The 31-year-old goalkeeper, who agreed to join the Catalan club in June from Real Sociedad, will undergo a medical and sign his contract on Monday before holding a press conference. After returning to Spain following Chile’s penalty shootout loss to Brazil last week, Bravo posed for photos in front of the club’s crest on Sunday. His contract runs until 2018. Bravo, who played 237 times for Real Sociedad over eight seasons and earned 83 caps for Chile, will compete for the starting goalkeeper position alongside fellow new signing Marc-André ter Stegen, replacing the departed Victor Valdés. Barcelona officially announced the four-year deal on Twitter, describing Bravo as a goalkeeper who 'offers agility and experience.' Bravo impressed during the World Cup, notably keeping a clean sheet in Chile’s 2-0 victory over Spain and denying Xabi Alonso in the match that eliminated Spain from the group stage. He has been captain of the Chilean national team since 2008 and began his professional career at Chilean club Colo-Colo. His move to Barcelona also reunites him with compatriot Alexis Sánchez. Bravo joins Barcelona as their third major signing of the summer, with Liverpool striker Luis Suárez rumored to be next. During his time at Real Sociedad, he experienced both relegation from La Liga in 2007 and Champions League qualification in 2013.

article_content: Jack Hutton-Potts, 23, died in a climbing accident off the coast of Anglesey, Wales, after falling from Gogarth Cliffs while roped to Vaughan Holme, the teacher who had introduced him to the sport. The two men, both experienced and safety-conscious climbers, plummeted more than 300 feet to their deaths in June 2013. They had met at Christ’s Hospital School in Horsham, West Sussex, where Holme, a 48-year-old housemaster and father of two, had mentored students in climbing. At the time of the accident, they were attempting The Gauntlet route at Gogarth Cliffs near Holyhead. It appears neither had secured their ropes to the cliff using safety equipment. The coroner noted that the cause of Holme’s initial fall remains unclear, but the lack of protective gear meant the fall was fatal for both. Pathologist Dr. Mark Lord stated that Hutton-Potts suffered a severe head injury and drowned instantly upon hitting the water. Holme died from multiple traumatic injuries. Elfyn Jones of the Llanberis Mountain Rescue Team suggested a possible judgment error regarding the use of a belay device, which might have prevented the fall’s catastrophic outcome. Lifeboats and an RAF helicopter participated in the search. An abseiling rescuer later identified impact marks consistent with Holme’s helmet. Catherine Butters, a former student taught by Holme, described him as 'very safe, very careful.' Christ’s Hospital School, founded in the 16th century, offers nearly 70% of its places through charitable funding, despite annual boarding fees of £28,000. Headmaster John Franklin said the school community was deeply shocked and saddened by the loss of a beloved teacher and a promising former student.

article_content: Anthony Marshall, the son of renowned philanthropist Brooke Astor, has died at age 90 in New York. Once a decorated World War II veteran, U.S. diplomat, and Broadway producer, Marshall spent time in prison in 2013 after being convicted of looting his mother’s $200 million estate during her battle with Alzheimer’s disease. Prosecutors revealed that while Astor’s cognitive abilities declined, Marshall transferred her assets to himself — purchasing a $920,000 yacht, removing valuable artworks from her home, and rewriting her will to divert millions away from cherished charities like the New York Public Library and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. His sons, Philip and Alec Marshall, testified against him in 2009, alleging both financial fraud and emotional neglect. Though physical neglect claims were never proven in court, they triggered the criminal investigation. Marshall was sentenced to one to three years in prison but was granted medical parole in August 2013 after being diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. He had previously appealed his sentence for years, citing a difficult childhood and poor health. In a cryptic obituary published in the New York Times by his wife, Charlene Marshall, no mention was made of Brooke Astor or his two sons. Instead, the tribute highlighted his decades of public service — including roles as U.S. Ambassador to Madagascar, Kenya, and Trinidad and Tobago (a combined posting), his work as a wildlife photographer and author of seven books, and his deep bond with his stepchildren, Arden, Inness, and Robert. Marshall acknowledged in a parole board interview that he remembered the crimes 'all too well,' and expressed regret, while also insisting he loved his mother and shared a strong sense of humor with her. He had paid $14.5 million in restitution to compensate for stolen funds. Brooke Astor, who died in 2007 at age 105, was celebrated for her generosity and awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Her final years, allegedly spent in squalor — sleeping in urine-soaked bedding and eating pureed food — stood in stark contrast to her lifelong legacy of giving.

article_content: I’m not a Disney theme park influencer, nor do I receive perks or free access from Disney — so I wasn’t officially given their new 'Brand Guidelines for Influencers.' But I managed to get my hands on a copy, and the rules are absurdly unrealistic. Even Disney itself routinely breaks them — often proudly and publicly. For instance, the guidelines forbid influencers from mentioning or depicting alcohol. Yet every year, EPCOT hosts its famous Food and Wine Festival, where premium wines and cocktails are central to the experience. Alcohol is also served at countless restaurants and bars across Disney parks worldwide. Even classic attractions like Pirates of the Caribbean and The Carousel of Progress feature animatronic characters drinking or smoking. The rules also ban guns or ammunition. But how do you explain Pirates of the Caribbean — a ride where guests are surrounded by cannon fire and swashbuckling pirates? Or the Frontierland Shootin’ Arcade, where kids are handed replica rifles? Disney doesn’t just allow this — it markets it. Violence and warfare? Disney’s $2 billion Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge land immerses guests in an intergalactic war, complete with lightsaber duels and toy sales. Even kid-friendly rides like Peter Pan’s Flight and Snow White’s Enchanted Wish include sword fights and magical confrontations. Politics and activism? Disney’s Hall of Presidents addresses slavery and the Civil War. Pandora – The World of Avatar promotes environmentalism and indigenous rights. During Pride Month, Disney sells rainbow-themed merchandise. According to the guidelines, influencers shouldn’t talk about any of this — but ignoring it means ignoring the park’s actual identity. Other banned categories are equally contradictory: no parodies of Disney characters? But Disney itself parodies itself constantly. No content that frightens children? Then how do you justify The Haunted Mansion? No sensationalism? Yet the entire business model thrives on spectacle. The truth? If influencers followed these rules literally, they’d only be allowed to film Winnie the Pooh — except even there, Pooh holds a toy gun, and in the original Dumbo film, the elephant flies after accidentally drinking champagne. In short: the guidelines are a joke. Disney knows it. Everyone else does too.

article_content: The Mississippi NAACP has urged Governor Haley Barbour to publicly reject a proposal by the Sons of Confederate Veterans (SCV) to feature Confederate General Nathan Bedford Forrest on a state specialty license plate. Forrest, a prominent and deeply controversial figure, served as the first Grand Wizard of the Ku Klux Klan — a white supremacist organization responsible for terrorizing Black Americans in the post-Civil War South. He is also linked to the 1864 Fort Pillow massacre, in which hundreds of Black Union soldiers were killed after surrendering — an event still debated by historians. Derrick Johnson, president of the Mississippi NAACP, condemned the plan, stating that anyone who betrayed the U.S. Constitution and promoted racial hatred must be held accountable. 'Forrest was a terrorist,' Johnson said. 'Honoring him sends a message of exclusion and hate.' More than 1,700 Mississippi residents have joined a Facebook group, 'Mississippians Against The Commemoration Of Grand Wizard Nathan Forrest,' which insists the state must not glorify a leader of the KKK. The SCV defends its choice, arguing that Forrest should be honored for his Civil War leadership, not his brief tenure with the Klan. Member Greg Stewart claims Forrest was unfairly maligned. Historians like Mike Martinez acknowledge that while Forrest left the KKK in 1869, citing its disorganization and unchecked violence, his association gave the group early credibility. The proposed license plate is part of a series of five Confederate-themed designs under review by the state legislature. Other images include Beauvoir (the Jefferson Davis Home), the Battle of Vicksburg, the Battle of Shiloh, and Confederate soldiers. One unexpected inclusion is Holt Collier, an African American who fought for the Confederacy and later became a famed bear hunter under President Theodore Roosevelt — a connection that led to the creation of the 'Teddy Bear.' The SCV has issued specialty plates since 2003, previously featuring a small Confederate flag, now redesigned. Proceeds support the restoration of historical state flags. Governor Barbour has not publicly responded to the controversy, despite rising media attention and calls for action. He recently spoke at the Conservative Political Action Conference in Washington, D.C., where he placed 15th in a straw poll — fueling speculation about a potential 2012 presidential bid.

article_content: As millions kick off their New Year’s health goals, many are rushing to buy juicers — often influenced by celebrities like Miranda Kerr and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley, who swear by their expensive Vitamix blenders priced at £500. But according to consumer testing by Which?, you don’t need to spend a fortune. In fact, models like the Philips HR1861, costing just under £70, outperformed pricier machines in lab tests for juice yield, ease of use, and cleaning. The Samson 6-in-1 and Philips Whole Fruit Juicer also ranked highly, proving that affordability doesn’t mean compromise. These celebrities aren’t just sipping smoothies for looks — they’re tapping into real nutritional science. Their signature green blends, packed with spinach, kale, cucumber, avocado, and chlorella, deliver a powerful mix of vitamins, minerals, and fiber. Chlorella, a Japanese algae supplement, offers iron equal to nine cups of spinach and B12 matching a 32oz steak — making it a convenient boost for busy lifestyles. Nutrition experts agree: the real magic lies in the ingredients, not the gadget. Leafy greens are among the most nutrient-rich foods on earth, rich in magnesium (a natural relaxant) and B12 (which fights fatigue). Blending them — even with a basic machine — helps you absorb more nutrients than eating them raw, while the fiber and water content keeps you full and reduces sugar cravings. Still, experts caution against impulse buys. Many kitchen gadgets end up gathering dust. Before investing, ask: Will I use this daily? Do I have space? Is my goal to drink more veggies — not own a status symbol? The Vitamix may be sleek and powerful, but it’s not essential. What matters is consistency. Whether you use a £60 blender or a hand-held immersion mixer, the key is filling your glass with greens — not marketing hype.

article_content: On January 16, 2013, Google honored Frank Zamboni—the innovator of the world’s first self-propelled ice-resurfacing machine—with a playful and interactive doodle marking his 112th birthday. Known for celebrating holidays and historical milestones, Google’s doodles often delight users, but this one left many puzzled. The animated game lets players drive a Zamboni machine across an ice rink, chasing away cartoon skaters to smooth the surface—a nod to Zamboni’s real-life invention. Born in 1901 to Italian immigrants in Utah, Zamboni moved with his family to Los Angeles, where he and his brothers ran an auto repair shop and later opened an electrical supply business. In 1927, they entered the block ice industry and opened an ice rink just before World War II. Frustrated by the labor-intensive process of maintaining smooth ice, Zamboni developed a solution: a machine that could resurface ice efficiently. He patented his design in 1946, but his true breakthrough came in 1949 with a fully self-contained machine that completed the task in just 10 minutes—down from 90 minutes and three workers. Zamboni’s invention transformed ice rinks worldwide. His company, now known as the Zamboni Company, has sold over 10,000 units. He passed away in 1988 at age 87, leaving behind a legacy that still glides across rinks today.

article_content: MEXICO CITY — Hurricane Lidia dissipated on Wednesday after making landfall as a Category 4 storm near the resort town of Puerto Vallarta, Mexico. The storm brought destructive winds up to 140 mph (220 kph), toppling trees, ripping roofs from homes, and triggering dangerous flooding. Authorities confirmed three fatalities: one person was killed by a falling tree on the northern outskirts of Puerto Vallarta; another drowned while attempting to cross a swollen river south of the landfall zone late Tuesday night; and two others sustained injuries in the affected areas. Laura Velázquez, head of Mexico’s civil defense system, reported the tree-related fatality and injuries, while Jalisco Governor Enrique Alfaro confirmed the drowning incident. Victor Hugo Romo of Jalisco’s civil defense office noted widespread roof damage in nearby communities. According to the U.S. National Hurricane Center, Lidia weakened rapidly after landfall, dropping to 35 mph (57 kph) as it dissipated about 145 miles (235 km) north-northeast of Guadalajara — Mexico’s second-largest city and capital of Jalisco. Lidia first made landfall on the sparsely populated Cabo Corrientes peninsula on Tuesday, then moved inland south of Puerto Vallarta with sustained winds of 105 mph (165 kph). Even after crossing land, it retained enough strength to briefly block several highways. In response, Jalisco state opened 23 emergency shelters, and Puerto Vallarta’s municipal government reported that dozens of residents sought refuge there. Nearby Nayarit state also recorded downed trees and localized damage. This event follows closely on the heels of Tropical Storm Max, which struck the southern Pacific coast in Guerrero state days earlier, washing out part of a coastal highway. The region has experienced similar devastation before: in 2015, Hurricane Patricia — a historic Category 5 storm — made landfall along the same remote stretch of coastline between Puerto Vallarta and Manzanillo. Meanwhile, in the Atlantic, Tropical Storm Sean formed far offshore with winds of 40 mph (65 kph), located roughly 780 miles (1,260 km) west-southwest of the Cape Verde Islands. Forecasters expect Sean to weaken into a tropical depression next week without threatening any landmass.

article_content: Yaya Touré has expressed regret for the victims and their families following last week’s deadly attack on the French satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo in Paris. The Manchester City midfielder and practicing Muslim apologized on behalf of his faith, saying he was 'afraid of what is going to happen' to innocent Muslims in the aftermath. Twelve people were killed when two armed assailants stormed the magazine’s offices. Speaking to CNN World Sport in early January, Touré said: 'When you hear something like that, it’s a big disappointment. I feel very sorry for the families — they lost their friend, their father, or their husband. I have a friend in Paris who is also Muslim, and I’m afraid of what is going to happen.' He added: 'Everybody has their point of view — everybody has something to say about it. It’s a newspaper trying to say something, but sometimes it hurts people.' Touré criticized the magazine’s depictions of the Prophet Muhammad as deeply offensive, yet affirmed his belief in freedom of speech. 'As a Muslim, I always believe in the right of people to say what they want,' he said. 'But sometimes newspapers go too far and do so without respect.' He noted that before the attack, some people had tried to peacefully urge Charlie Hebdo to stop publishing such cartoons. 'Afterwards, we heard about these people doing horrible things.' Touré, a four-time African Player of the Year, has scored nine goals in 26 appearances for Manchester City this season.

article_content: Nafissatou Diallo, the Guinean hotel maid who accused former International Monetary Fund (IMF) chief Dominique Strauss-Kahn of sexual assault in a New York hotel room, has broken her silence and spoken publicly for the first time. In interviews with Newsweek and ABC News’s Robin Roberts, Diallo recounted the traumatic incident that occurred on May 14 at the Sofitel Hotel, where she worked. CNN, which previously withheld her name in accordance with its policy of not identifying sexual assault victims, has now named her following her decision to go public. Diallo described how Strauss-Kahn, naked and aggressive, forcibly confined her in his luxury suite, attempted to force her to perform oral sex, and later dismissed her with threats. 'Because of him, they call me a prostitute,' she said, referencing false rumors spread in media reports. 'I want him to go to jail. I want him to know there are some places you cannot use your power, you cannot use your money.' Strauss-Kahn, 62, was arrested at JFK Airport while boarding a flight to Paris and charged with sexual abuse and attempted rape. He pleaded not guilty. Initially held on $6 million bail and later confined to a luxury townhouse under house arrest, he was released in July after prosecutors revealed inconsistencies in Diallo’s statements regarding her whereabouts after the incident and details in her asylum and tax documents. Though the case has weakened procedurally, charges remain active. Meanwhile, new allegations surfaced in France: writer Tristane Banon accused Strauss-Kahn of attempted rape in 2003; he has since filed a counter-claim against her for false declarations. Public tensions escalated as Strauss-Kahn’s U.S.-based attorneys, William Taylor and Benjamin Brafman, accused Diallo and her legal team of orchestrating a media campaign to pressure prosecutors and extract financial compensation. 'It is time for this unseemly circus to stop,' they declared. In response, Diallo’s attorney, Kenneth Thompson, condemned the attacks as an 'unprecedented smear campaign' against a victim of violent sexual assault. 'Because of those contemptible, baseless and anonymous attacks, Ms. Diallo was forced to come forward in order to put a face to the brutal crime,' he said. The next court hearing is scheduled for August 1. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office, citing the need to preserve judicial integrity, declined to comment on the specifics of the ongoing investigation. 'We will not discuss the facts or evidence,' said spokesperson Erin Duggan.

article_content: Myanmar President Thein Sein declared a state of emergency on Tuesday in the Kokang region, where clashes have erupted between rebel forces and government troops. He made the announcement on state television, stating that martial law would be imposed in the Kokang self-administered zone for three months, effective immediately. Last week, state media reported that days of fighting with Kokang rebels had left 47 government soldiers dead and dozens more wounded. Kokang forces suffered losses in territory and personnel during a 2009 military offensive, but have since regrouped. They are one of several ethnic minority groups in Myanmar seeking greater autonomy. The rebels have not agreed to sign the nationwide peace accord the government has been negotiating with other armed ethnic groups. Under Thein Sein’s order, the commander-in-chief of Myanmar’s military now holds full authority over the region’s administrative functions, community peace, rule of law, and judicial matters. CNN’s Jethro Mullen and Mitra Mobasherat contributed to this report.

These revelations came to light following a university task force investigation launched in February 2012 after two players were charged with sexual assault. The investigation uncovered a troubling culture of sexual entitlement among some athletes, with multiple accounts indicating that players believed consent was unnecessary, especially when intoxicated. One female student reported that a player forcibly touched her while she punched him in protest, yet he continued. When asked why she didn't report it, she replied, 'That’s just what BU hockey players do.' Players also publicly boasted about their sexual encounters on Facebook, referring to partners as 'kills.' Beer kegs were consumed in locker room showers, and the full extent of the party’s chaos remained unknown to campus authorities until the investigation began. Coach Jack Parker initially claimed ignorance of the event but later admitted he knew some players had been drinking in the locker room. However, multiple sources confirmed he reprimanded the team within days. Academically, several hockey players were described as disruptive in class — intimidating peers and using phones during lectures — leading six to drop the course. Yet other professors noted some players were respectful and diligent. The university has accepted 14 recommendations from the task force, including stripping Parker of his title as Executive Athletic Director. He remains head coach with unchanged salary.

article_content: According to Russian government reports, more than half of the Russian soldiers injured in the ongoing conflict in Ukraine have lost one or more limbs, a statistic described by Deputy Labor Minister Alexey Vovchenko as 'a glaring issue.' In remarks made during a Federation Council roundtable on soldier rehabilitation, Vovchenko noted that approximately 54% of wounded troops undergoing medical care have undergone amputations — a rate far higher than what is seen among disabled civilians in Russia. Of these cases, about one in five involves the loss of an upper limb. To support recovery, each injured soldier is typically prescribed an average of three assistive devices, including prosthetics, wheelchairs, custom orthopedic footwear, and specialized clothing. Government officials say arrangements for full rehabilitation programs are already being implemented. Meanwhile, U.S. intelligence estimates suggest that since Russia’s full-scale invasion began in February 2022, nearly half a million military personnel from both sides have been killed or wounded, with Russian losses alone approaching 300,000 — including roughly 120,000 fatalities and 180,000 injuries.

article_content: (CNN) — Defending champions Real Madrid trail their arch-rivals Barcelona by 18 points in La Liga, so for the remainder of the season, their focus has shifted to cup competitions. The massive gap has intensified pressure on coach José Mourinho, who must now prioritize Spain’s premier cup tournament, the Copa del Rey, and the UEFA Champions League to salvage the campaign. All might be forgiven if he secures Europe’s most prestigious club trophy for a third time as a manager — having previously won it with Portuguese side Porto and Italian giants Inter Milan. At minimum, Real’s fans expect him to lift Spain’s second-most important domestic honor. A 2-0 victory in the first leg of their Copa del Rey tie helped quiet the growing protests against him. Karim Benzema opened the scoring in the 37th minute, converting a pass from German international Sami Khedira, followed by an own goal from Valencia’s Andrés Guardado, sealing the win on a chilly night in Madrid. Real Madrid rode their luck on multiple occasions in front of their passionate home crowd. Cristiano Ronaldo, as usual, led their attacking efforts early on, firing a free kick just wide. Luka Modrić, signed last year from Tottenham Hotspur, missed a golden opportunity to put Real ahead. Valencia’s Brazilian striker Jonas came close twice in quick succession, but his misses proved costly. Around the 60th minute, Valencia dominated play, and Jonas squandered a clear chance, shooting wide from 12 yards after Iker Casillas parried Roberto Soldado’s shot into his path. Yet again, Real capitalized on Valencia’s error: Guardado inadvertently deflected Fabio Coentrao’s cross into his own net. Ronaldo was denied his 29th goal of the season by two outstanding saves from Valencia goalkeeper Vicente, who first blocked a point-blank shot from ten yards and then tipped a powerful strike onto the post less than a minute later. The 2-0 result gives Real a strong advantage heading into the return leg in Valencia next Wednesday. In the Coppa Italia, Inter Milan edged past Bologna 3-2 thanks to a stoppage-time winner in extra time. Goals from Fredy Guarin and Rodrigo Palacio gave Inter a commanding lead, but Alessandro Diamanti and Manolo Gabbiadini scored twice in four minutes to force extra time. Andrea Ranocchia’s header in the 120th minute crushed Bologna’s hopes and sent Inter through to the semifinals. In England’s FA Cup, Premier League sides Wigan Athletic, Queens Park Rangers, Stoke City, and Fulham all won their replays, while Sunderland were eliminated by second-tier Bolton Wanderers.

article_content: A Tampa, Florida police captain exclaimed, 'I can't believe what I've done,' after fatally shooting a fellow moviegoer for texting, according to a witness. Alan Hamilton, a deputy from Sumter County, was inside the West Chapel theater during a screening of Lone Survivor when he witnessed 71-year-old retired police officer Curtis Reeves shoot and kill 43-year-old Chad Oulson. Witnesses provided accounts in Pasco County Court as Reeves sought release on bail. He has been held without bond since the January 13 shooting. Witness Mark Turner said he overheard Oulson ask Reeves to stop texting, saying, 'Do you mind? I’ve got a voicemail from my babysitter—I’d like to check if my daughter is okay.' After further requests, Oulson stood up and tossed a small bag of popcorn at Reeves. Turner stated, 'Almost immediately, the gun came out, the shot was fired, and it went back into Mr. Reeves’ lap.' Hamilton testified that after the shooting, Reeves told his wife, 'You shut your [expletive] mouth and don’t say another word,' after she remarked, 'That was no cause to shoot anyone.' Reeves pleaded not guilty to second-degree murder. His defense argues he acted in self-defense, claiming Oulson committed battery by throwing an object—specifically popcorn—and that Reeves, due to his age, deserves special legal consideration. Hamilton and Turner both reported seeing no injury on Reeves’ face and no evidence that Oulson punched or struck him. Reeves’ daughter, Jennifer Shaw, 40, testified that her father was devoted to family, attended church weekly, and that all firearms had been removed from their home by her brother, a Tampa police officer. The family offered their $186,000 home as collateral for bail. Thomas DePolis, a former colleague who helped Reeves establish the Tampa SWAT team, stated, 'There’s nothing in my experience with him that suggests he’s dangerous.' Nicole Oulson, Chad’s widow, expressed heartbreak, saying she wants Reeves imprisoned for life. Their 22-month-old daughter, Lexy, lost her father. The judge declined to rule on bail today but ordered that theater surveillance footage be shown in court and released publicly 30 days after the trial concludes. Florida law, amended in 2011, prohibits public access to videos depicting homicides, even under its otherwise expansive public records rules.

article_content: (CNN) — Japan winger Shinji Kagawa scored for Borussia Dortmund in a 1-0 victory over Bayer Leverkusen on Saturday, keeping the reigning champions at the top of the Bundesliga. The Japanese forward netted from a tight angle just before halftime, marking his fourth goal in four consecutive games. The win extended Dortmund’s lead to two points over Bayern Munich, who secured a comfortable 2-0 win against Kaiserslautern. Goals from Mario Gomez in the sixth minute and Thomas Müller in the 30th minute sealed the victory. Mid-table Stuttgart crushed 10-man Hertha Berlin 5-0. Austria striker Martin Harnik scored a first-half brace after Vedad Ibisevic opened the scoring, with Shinji Okazaki adding another goal before the break. Hertha’s Andreas Ottl was sent off in the first half for a foul on Hungarian midfielder Tamás Hajnal. Georgian defender Levan Kobiashvili compounded Hertha’s misery with an own goal in the 59th minute. Hoffenheim’s new coach Markus Babbel, who replaced the recently dismissed Holger Stanislawski, earned his first point with a 1-1 draw at Werder Bremen. Marko Arnautović equalized for Bremen in stoppage time after Danish defender Jannik Vestergaard had given Hoffenheim a fourth-minute lead. Hannover salvaged a point in their match against Mainz thanks to an injury-time goal by Polish striker Artur Sobiech, after Mohamed Zidan had put the hosts ahead in the seventh minute.

article_content: A 34-year-old woman, Kerry Blenkinsopp, has been jailed for stealing £2,600 from her disabled mother, Rosina, who was saving the money for essential home adaptations following a stroke and subsequent wheelchair confinement. Blenkinsopp took £800 from a safe under her mother’s bed and later stole another £1,800 while her mother was attending physiotherapy. She then falsely reported a burglary to conceal her crimes. She admitted to spending the money on items including a £200 iPad, a washing machine, a cooker, and a car — which she described as 'basics' for her new home. At Teesside Crown Court, Judge John Walford condemned the act as a 'dreadful betrayal of trust,' emphasizing that the stolen funds were specifically intended to make her mother’s home accessible. The judge imposed an eight-month prison sentence, stating that any lesser punishment would outrage the family and fail to reflect the severity of the emotional and financial harm inflicted. Since the thefts in July, Rosina Blenkinsopp has severed all ties with her daughter and obtained a restraining order to prevent contact. In a victim impact statement, Rosina tearfully declared, 'I want nothing more to do with her.' Blenkinsopp, who is unemployed, pleaded guilty to two counts of theft and one count of wasting police time. Her defense solicitor stated she wishes to repay her mother and reconcile, though her family has made clear they do not wish to reconnect.

article_content: By Sarah Griffiths. A toddler born with a rare hip condition is now walking — and even running — after wearing a custom plaster cast, nicknamed 'concrete trousers'. Harrison Hobson was diagnosed with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) shortly after birth, a condition where the hip joint fails to form properly, causing frequent dislocations. At just four days old, he was placed in a full-body harness to stabilize his hips. When this conservative treatment proved insufficient, surgeons operated at five weeks old, placing his legs in a plaster cast. The first cast failed after one week, prompting a second, more invasive surgery and a new cast. For over three months, his mother, Charlotte Hobson, navigated the challenges of bathing, dressing, and holding him while he was immobilized. Guidance from the charity Steps helped the family learn safe ways to carry Harrison — avoiding lifting under the armpits due to the cast’s weight. They were also reassured that others would respond with empathy once they understood the condition. Initially, Charlotte feared Harrison would lag behind peers in reaching milestones. But at 14 months, he took his first steps. Now, at age two, he runs around like any other energetic toddler. Charlotte described the cast as 'a pair of concrete trousers' — bulky, uncomfortable, and socially conspicuous. She worried strangers might mock her son, especially after reading every parenting book during pregnancy and finding no mention of DDH. Doctors initially suspected both hips were affected, but later confirmed only the right hip was dislocated. Her husband Jason, a professional rugby player, assumed it was a simple joint issue — until he learned DDH requires long-term intervention. Tim McLachlan, CEO of Steps, notes that many families face insensitive questions like, 'How did you break both their legs?' — revealing widespread public unawareness. DDH affects 1–3% of UK births annually — up to 24,000 children — more than new cases of leukaemia and skin cancer combined. Thanks to early diagnosis and persistent care, Harrison has made a full recovery. Today, there’s no trace of his struggle — only a happy, active child.

article_content: After 40 days of coordinated strikes, the United Auto Workers (UAW) secured a landmark breakthrough in its dispute with Ford, General Motors, and Stellantis. On Wednesday, the union announced a tentative agreement with Ford granting workers a 25% pay increase — the largest raise in over two decades. This victory came after workers walked off the job and took to the picket lines across key manufacturing plants. The UAW employed a smart, phased strategy known as the 'stand-up strike': instead of shutting down every plant at once, it targeted the most profitable facilities to maximize economic pressure while prolonging the disruption. This approach caught competitors off guard — Stellantis reportedly prepared for walkouts at plants that were never hit. The pressure intensified when workers struck a Stellantis plant in Sterling Heights, Michigan, on Monday, followed by 5,000 GM employees walking out in Arlington, Texas, on Tuesday. UAW President Shawn Fain said these were the automakers’ most profitable sites. 'Ford knew what was coming for them on Wednesday if we didn’t get a deal,' he said. 'That was checkmate.' Despite the Ford deal, both GM and Stellantis held firm initially. On Tuesday, GM CEO Mary Barra stated during an earnings call that her company had made a record pay offer and would not accept a contract that endangered its future. Barra, who earns approximately $29 million annually — up a third in four years — was among the highest-paid CEOs in the industry. Negotiations between the UAW and GM continued until 5 a.m. Thursday, with Reuters reporting the two sides were nearly aligned on financial terms but still debating issues like temporary worker usage. Similar talks were underway with Stellantis. As the strikes neared a potential end after six weeks, Senator Bernie Sanders urged GM and Stellantis to 'get serious and negotiate a fair contract.' He added, 'When workers fight back against corporate greed, they win. The American people are watching.' Fain echoed the sentiment, posting: 'Don’t let them tell you it can’t be done. The working class is going on offense — and winning.' This momentum mirrors a recent victory by the Teamsters Union, which secured a deal allowing full-time UPS drivers to earn up to $170,000 annually — a figure so impressive it drew envy even from tech workers. With over 340,000 unionized UPS employees ready to strike, the company chose to negotiate rather than risk massive disruption. In contrast, the Big Three automakers endured prolonged, highly visible labor actions that disrupted production. The message to corporate America is clear: underestimating organized labor is no longer an option.

article_content: In the quiet village of Holt, northern Germany, a three-year-old Arabian horse named Nasar has become an unlikely houseguest — and his owner wouldn’t have it any other way. After seeking shelter from the violent Storm Xaver in December 2013, Nasar simply never left. Now, he spends his days lounging inside the thatched cottage of Dr. Stephanie Arndt, a 39-year-old physician who treats him less like livestock and more like a moody teenager. Nasar has developed habits that would make any adolescent proud: he stares endlessly at his reflection, taps out melodies on the piano with his nose, and politely — if messily — begs for glasses of juice. He’s even learned to nap beside his owner on the couch, despite his towering frame. The only real damage he’s caused? A single cracked mug, which earned him a firm scolding — and, so far, no repeat offenses. While most horses graze in pastures, Nasar shows little interest in his outdoor pen. 'He doesn’t like wind or rain,' Arndt explains. 'He thinks the house is perfect.' She adds that he chooses to come in — and often, he won’t let her forget it. When he wants into the living room, he waits patiently at the door. Once inside, he claims the space like a king. And yes, he does sometimes get startled if someone sneaks up behind him — just like a teen who hates being poked. Though he’s technically an animal, Nasar’s quirks feel oddly familiar. His grey-tipped mane? Check. Obsession with mirrors? Double check. Refusing to tidy up? Absolutely. Arndt laughs off comparisons to a teenager — but admits, 'He’s got personality. And he knows it.'

article_content: After eight harrowing days stranded at sea, two Bahamian fishermen—Anthony Douglas, 57, and Mike Russell, 58—have recounted their astonishing survival story. Their 16-foot fishing boat capsized during a sudden storm on September 7, 2013, leaving them clinging to its hull in open waters off the Florida coast. With no food or fresh water, they survived by sucking on seaweed, taking brief naps in shifts, and constantly praying. Douglas described how the storm hit without warning: 'One moment it was calm, the next, waves came from every direction.' After being thrown into the ocean, he swam to Russell, who was sinking, and pulled him onto the wreckage. For days, they endured hallucinations, talking to imaginary people and pretending to eat meals they didn’t have. On the sixth day, Russell, weakened and desperate, jumped back into the sea, telling Douglas, 'I’m holding you back—you can make it alone.' Douglas dove after him, dragged him back, tied their shirts together, and refused to let go. 'Keep praying,' he told him. 'Pray from your heart, not just your lips.' They were spotted by a passing freighter on September 14, which alerted the US Coast Guard. A helicopter airlifted them to safety. Medics at Delray Beach Medical Center found them severely dehydrated, with raw, sunburned skin and salt-damaged hands from gripping the fiberglass hull. Rescue swimmer Kyle Stallings said they were 'completely waterlogged' and visibly fading—'on their last straw of hope.' Against all odds, they lived. Most humans cannot survive more than three days without water.

article_content: Ben Ford is a towering figure — big beard, broad shoulders, and an unmistakable presence. He jokes that he’s the spitting image of his father, Harrison Ford, and believes his dad would look just like him if he hadn’t spent decades on Hollywood’s restrictive diets. Both men share a deep love for food. For Ben, cooking isn’t just a job — it’s a ritual. He thrives on hearty, meat-heavy meals, sizzling barbecues, and mountains of potatoes. His new cookbook, 'Taming The Feast,' with its step-by-step guide to building a barbecue from scratch, might just be the most ruggedly masculine cookbook ever written. We’re at Ford’s Filling Station in Los Angeles, Ben’s restaurant, where every dish carries decades of experience — and a secret ingredient he credits to his mother, Mary Marquardt, a former cheerleader whose home cooking left an indelible mark. Ben’s mission? To inspire a new generation of men to gather around the fire, cook for crowds, and recreate the joy of long, loud dinners filled with food and laughter. Most recipes serve eight to ten people, echoing the memories of family tables stacked high and glasses overflowing. At 46, Ben is the eldest of Harrison Ford’s four children — two from his marriage to Mary, two from his union with screenwriter Melissa Mathison. His parents divorced when Ben was 12, just as Harrison’s acting career began to soar. For much of Ben’s childhood, his father worked as a carpenter, fixing up homes and taking Ben along to construction sites, teaching him precision and patience — lessons Ben now applies in the kitchen. Though Harrison’s fame changed their lives — and eventually led to a second marriage with Calista Flockhart in 2010 — Ben insists they were never estranged. Harrison and Calista, along with her son Liam, regularly visit the restaurant. ‘We get along great,’ Ben says. He recalls a quieter upbringing: ‘There weren’t so many celebrity friends when my parents were together.’ Ben found unexpected mentorship in his stepfather, Bob Becker, a TV director who loved to cook. ‘I got the best of both worlds,’ he says. Even as Harrison traveled the globe filming blockbusters — including the latest Star Wars movie, where he broke his leg during production of 'Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny' in 2022 — Ben says his father remained a steady presence. He gave Harrison a copy of his book for Father’s Day. ‘I hope he’s trying out some recipes this summer,’ Ben says with a smile. ‘He doesn’t cook like I do.’ Ben once dreamed of playing professional baseball until a devastating knee injury ended that path. He turned to cooking at a time when kitchens were brutal, aggressive places. ‘It took grit,’ he says. ‘You’re on your feet 14 to 16 hours a day, six days a week. Not everyone can handle it.’ His personal life includes a 13-year-old son, Ethan, from his first marriage, and a four-year-old son, Waylon, with his current wife, Emily, who works alongside him. Growing up with a famous father brought pressure — and skepticism. ‘People doubted I was serious,’ he admits. ‘They thought, “He doesn’t need this.”’ But he learned to embrace the spotlight without letting it define him. One of his earliest memories — watching a whole pig roast on a Hawaiian beach — sparked his signature dish. Another came during visits to Elstree Studios, where he wandered film sets and soaked in Sunday roasts at cast members’ homes. He was among the first in LA to serve whole-animal cuisine and hire foragers — trends now celebrated across the city. Yet none of it would exist without his mother’s cooking. Her simple roast chicken remains unmatched. ‘I’ve tried for 28 years. I still can’t replicate it,’ he says quietly. ‘She still makes it.’ Mary, who lives with progressive multiple sclerosis, remains a quiet pillar of strength. ‘Food is love in our house,’ Ben says. ‘My mom’s chicken kept us together through everything.’ Despite their divorce, Mary and Harrison remain close — a bond Ben calls extraordinary. ‘She’s a truly special person.’ For Ben, no recipe, no accolade, no barbecue — not even the perfect smoked brisket — could ever top his mother’s roast chicken. And he wouldn’t want it to.
